## Personality

Susan is a grim-faced, gray, and gaunt handmaiden of the [Blythe](../character/blythe.md) family at [Ingleside](../codex/places.md#ingleside), known for being faithful, kind-hearted, and practical. Characterized as an elderly spinster, she holds a deep respect for the clergy and enjoys discussing funerals. She approaches life with a calm pragmatism, serenely doing what she can for humanity's betterment while leaving the rest to Higher Powers rather than trying to run the world. Unsentimental about literature, she views poetry as mostly composed of lies, though she insists on maintaining tradition by serving pudding on Sundays. Skilled at knitting, she harbors a constant fear that the children will poison themselves by eating roots gathered near the pond, and she intends to visit to view Rosemary's trousseau.

## History

Susan Baker, an un married woman who never had a beau, once had an uncle who began as a poet and ended up becoming a tramp. She returned from caring for a sick neighbor to work as hired help for [Anne](../character/anne.md) and [Gilbert](../character/gilbert-blythe.md), making an unconscious funny remark that sent [Gilbert](../character/gilbert-blythe.md) and Captain Jim outside laughing. Following the tragic loss of Anne's firstborn, [Gilbert](../character/gilbert-blythe.md) and Susan insisted that [Anne](../character/anne.md) keep Susan on as help for the summer so she could regain her health. Over the following years, Susan remained an integral part of the household, helping nurse [Anne](../character/anne.md) back to health after she gave birth to a healthy baby boy named [James Matthew](../character/james-a.md). After Susan's sister broke her leg, Susan temporarily left [Four Winds](../codex/places.md#four-winds) to tend to her, returning late from the [Glen](../codex/places.md#glen) with local news and expressing surprise at Miss Cornelia's impending marriage. When [Anne](../character/anne.md) and [Gilbert](../character/gilbert-blythe.md) later relocated their growing family from the house of dreams to the [Glen](../codex/places.md#glen), Susan moved with them to [Ingleside](../codex/places.md#ingleside). At [Ingleside](../codex/places.md#ingleside), Susan regularly conversed with [Anne](../character/anne.md) and Miss Cornelia, sharing local gossip while helping care for Anne's younger children, [Rilla](../character/rilla-blythe.md) and baby [Shirley](../character/shirley.md). When the Meredith children sprinted to [Ingleside](../codex/places.md#ingleside) terrified after mistaking a neighbor for a ghost, Susan soothed them and investigated the garden dyke armed with a pitchfork, later returning to reveal the embarrassing truth. She remained a steadfast presence at [Ingleside](../codex/places.md#ingleside), frequently discussing parish rumors, local scandals, and upcoming weddings with [Anne](../character/anne.md) and Miss Cornelia.

## Quotes

> "Have a good time and do not worry about the pantry. Susan is at the helm. There is no use in keeping a dog and doing your own barking. I am going to take your breakfast up to you every morning."
>
> — Susan — [v4 CHAPTER 22 MISS CORNELIA ARRANGES MATTERS P3](../source/v04-c22.md#nw-v04-c22-p0003)

> "If you cannot I will not go, Mrs. Doctor, dear, Matilda’s leg to the contrary notwithstanding. I will not have you worried, and that blessed child upset in consequence, for any number of legs."
>
> — Susan — [v4 CHAPTER 36 BEAUTY FOR ASHES P23](../source/v04-c36.md#nw-v04-c36-p0023)

> “I am afraid they love it too well,” said Susan gloomily. “Little Jem said once he would rather go to Rainbow Valley than to heaven when he died, and that was not a proper remark.”
>
> — Susan — [v5 CHAPTER II. SHEER GOSSIP P2](../source/v05-c02.md#nw-v05-c02-p0002)

> “He looked exactly like a great black tomcat, that he did, Mrs. Dr. dear,” said Susan. “I never could abide such a man in the pulpit every Sunday.”
>
> — Susan — [v5 CHAPTER II. SHEER GOSSIP P16](../source/v05-c02.md#nw-v05-c02-p0016)

> "If I felt I had any right to express an opinion concerning such a solemn matter as a minister’s marriage I would say that I think Elizabeth’s cousin Sarah, over-harbour, would make Mr. Meredith a better wife."
>
> — Susan — [v5 CHAPTER VII. A FISHY EPISODE P35](../source/v05-c07.md#nw-v05-c07-p0035)
